tldr: At the unconditional coverage threshold, high-saturation network experiments retain finitely many informative Bernoulli responses in a thin boundary layer. The sharp target is the minimax expected length of a connected confidence interval for the superpopulation full-rollout adoption mean. Its proposed frontier is the explicitly defined value \(H(s)=\phi(z)h(s+\gamma)\) of a harmonic connected-confidence game: binomial count-mark actions share an everywhere normalized \(90\%\) coverage budget with an escaped zero-information allocation whose cost is its integrated coverage profile. The theorem identifies this game with the original-binomial limit, evaluates it with convergent certified errors, and attains it with total original-record intervals having exact finite unconditional honesty. The graph and response law are random, under the supplied ER, IID-response, and zero-own-control adoption primitives.
